description:
Several gf2-core tests deviate from the project's test-naming and ignore-annotation conventions. Bring them into line so the suite reads uniformly and the slow tier is self-describing.

## Background

The project requires every ignored test to carry a tagged reason string and every test function to be named `test_<operation>_<scenario>`.

Two deviations exist in this crate. The wide-field axiom stress test at `crates/gf2-core/src/field/axiom_tests.rs:1027` uses a bare ignore attribute with no reason, unlike every other ignored test in the same file. Separately, four tests near `crates/gf2-core/src/bitvec.rs:1705` are named for the operation alone with no scenario suffix, and the same pattern repeats in the quadratic and cubic extension-field modules.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The wide-field axiom stress test carries a lowercase `slow:` tagged reason describing why it exceeds the fast tier.
- [hard] REQ-02: No bare ignore attribute remains anywhere in gf2-core.
- [hard] REQ-03: The four bit-vector tests and their counterparts in the quadratic and cubic extension modules are renamed to `test_<operation>_<scenario>`, where the scenario names the asserted outcome.
- [hard] REQ-04: Renamed tests assert the same behaviour as before; no test is dropped or weakened.
- [hard] REQ-05: The fast tier stays inside its per-test and whole-suite time budgets, and clippy with warnings denied plus formatting pass.
title: Bring gf2-core test names and ignore annotations to convention
